name: Livraria Lello
short: A neo-Gothic bookshop opened on 13 January 1906, with its forked red staircase and a skylight bearing the motto “Decus in Labore”.
long: Livraria Lello stands at 144 Rua das Carmelitas, a few steps from the Clérigos tower. The neo-Gothic building was designed by the engineer Francisco Xavier Esteves, and its opening on 13 January 1906 caused a stir in Porto’s cultural circles. The red staircase that forks into two flights and the stained-glass skylight by the Dutchman Van Krieken have made it one of the most photographed bookshops on earth. A local legend long tied the staircase to Harry Potter, but in 2020 J. K. Rowling denied it.
history:
The firm began in 1869, when the Frenchman Ernesto Chardron opened the “Livraria Internacional de Ernesto Chardron” at 96–98 Rua dos Clérigos. He was the first to publish much of Camilo Castelo Branco’s work and other major names of the age. After his death at 45 the house passed to “Lugan & Genelioux” and then to Mathieux Lugan alone; in 1891 Chardron absorbed the stock of three Porto bookshops.

In 1881 José Pinto de Sousa Lello opened a shop of his own at 18–20 Rua do Almada. On 30 June 1894 Mathieux Lugan sold him the old Livraria Chardron, and José, together with his brother António Lello, kept it under the name “Sociedade José Pinto Sousa Lello & Irmão”. In 1898 the stock of the Lemos bookshop joined the firm.

The new building, designed by the engineer Francisco Xavier Esteves, was inaugurated on 13 January 1906 at 144 Rua das Carmelitas. Among the guests were Guerra Junqueiro, Abel Botelho, João Grave, Bento Carqueja, Aurélio da Paz dos Reis, José Leite de Vasconcelos and Afonso Costa. In 1919 the firm became “Livraria Lello e Irmão, Lda.”, and since 1995 it has again been known simply as “Livraria Lello”.

The façade opens in a large segmental arch with a central door and two side windows; above are three rectangular windows flanked by painted figures of “Art” and “Science” by the Belgian Joseph Bielmann. Under carved canopies the sculptor Romão Júnior carved busts of Antero de Quental, Eça de Queirós, Camilo Castelo Branco, Teófilo Braga, Tomás Ribeiro and Guerra Junqueiro. The skylight (8 × 3.5 m, 55 glass panels) was made by the Dutchman Gerardus Samuel van Krieken and carries the shop’s monogram and motto, “Decus in Labore”.

For years it was said that the Lello staircase inspired Flourish and Blotts, where Harry Potter first meets Gilderoy Lockhart. J. K. Rowling lived in Porto in 1991–1993, but in May 2020 she stated that she had never entered Lello and that its staircase had not influenced Harry Potter.

The shop was modernised in 1995, and since 23 July 2015 entry has been ticketed, with the fee deducted from a book purchase. In 2016 the skylight was dismantled and restored for the first time since it was made. In 2019 the shop received 1.2 million visitors. A Livraria Lello Foundation was announced in 2024, and in 2026, for its 120th anniversary, a new wing by Álvaro Siza opened and the shop was reclassified as a national monument.
facts: Opened on 13 January 1906 at 144 Rua das Carmelitas.
The building was designed by the engineer Francisco Xavier Esteves.
The skylight (8 × 3.5 m, 55 panels) by Gerardus Samuel van Krieken bears the motto “Decus in Labore” (dignity in work).
Busts of six Portuguese writers were carved by the sculptor Romão Júnior.
Since 23 July 2015 entry has been ticketed, with the fee deducted from a book purchase.
In 2016 the skylight was dismantled for restoration for the first time since 1906.
It received 1.2 million visitors in 2019 and became a national monument in 2026.
tip: Come at opening time; by midday the queues are long. Entry is ticketed, but the fee is deducted from any book you buy. The shop is five minutes from São Bento station and the Clérigos tower, so combine it with the Carmo church across the street.
